panel.label: Experimental
panel.name: experimental
panel.string: [ENTRIES] textures, [USED] of [MAX] GB. This session: [LOADS] loaded, [STORES] stored, [REMOVED] removed.
panel.text: Experimental and diagnostic settings. Some changes require a viewer restart.

text.name: experimental_preset_label
text.tool_tip: Presets hold every setting on the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs. The General, Textures and Avatar tabs are not included.

combo_box.name: experimental_preset_combo
combo_box.tool_tip: Presets hold every setting on the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs; settings a preset doesn't list are set to their defaults when it is loaded. The General, Textures and Avatar tabs are not included. Built-in presets can't be changed or deleted; Cancel undoes a loaded preset.

button.label: Load
button.name: experimental_preset_load
button.tool_tip: Set the settings of the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs from the selected preset. Settings it doesn't list go back to their defaults. Cancel undoes it.

button.label: Save as...
button.name: experimental_preset_save
button.tool_tip: Save the current settings of the Photo, Effects, Rendering, Shadows and Performance tabs as a new preset, or replace one of your own.

button.label: Delete
button.name: experimental_preset_delete
button.tool_tip: Delete the selected preset. Only your own presets can be deleted.

view.name: experimental_indicator_legend
view.tool_tip: The marks beside each setting are a rough guide. The circle is what the option costs in frame time when it is on (or, for a value, when it is raised): blue saves time, green costs little, yellow some, red a lot. The square is how much it improves the picture: green a lot, yellow some, grey little or nothing (options for speed, loading or diagnostics). Real costs depend on the scene and the graphics card.

panel.name: experimental_general_settings

button.label: Suggest settings...
button.name: suggest_settings
button.tool_tip: Measure where the frame time goes in this scene for about 20 seconds and suggest settings to change, with the time each would save and what it would look like. Nothing changes until you apply a suggestion, and Undo puts the previous values back.

check_box.label: Game controller: left stick sets the speed, its button toggles run

The stick never starts a run by itself. Pressing the left stick (L3) toggles always-run, as long as nothing is bound to that button in the Game Control preferences. Does not affect the flycam, the keyboard or what is sent to the server. Debug settings FSGameControlSlowBelow and FSGameControlRunAt set the thresholds.

A ring around the mouse cursor fills while the button is held; let go before it is full to cancel. Movement, camera and flycam controls, the keyboard and the mouse are not affected. Debug setting FSGameControlHoldActions chooses which button actions have to be held.

check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. text.name: fs_fsrenderterrainantitiling_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Breaks up the visible repetition of the terrain textures, on legacy and PBR terrain. Macro variation: each texture is blended with a copy of itself at a much larger scale, by soft noise, with a slight brightness and hue jitter; one extra texture read per layer. Hex tiling: near the camera the texture is laid out on hexagonal cells, each shifted and turned at random and blended along the texture's own contrast, so no repeat is left to see; three reads per layer for colour and normal, macro variation beyond the distance below. Rebuilds shaders.

Instead of one pass per light, so places with many lights (clubs, events, cities at night) cost much less GPU and CPU time. Lighting should look the same. Projectors and spotlights are unchanged.

Each light gets a shadow map drawn from the light in all six directions, so walls, furniture and avatars block it wherever they are, on screen or not, with smooth edges that need no TAA. A map is only drawn again where something in it changes: a still room costs nothing to keep, avatars and moving objects near the light do. Needs shadows. Turning it on or off rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: Reverse-Z depth (no z-fighting far away)
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderreversez
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Stores depth with the near plane at 1 and the far plane at 0 in a 32 bit floating point depth buffer, which keeps depth precise all the way to the draw distance. Removes the flickering where distant surfaces meet (mainland at 500 m and more) and sharpens what reads depth far away: screen-space reflections, ambient occlusion and fog. Shadow maps are unchanged. Needs OpenGL 4.5; stays off on older drivers. Almost no GPU cost. Changing it rebuilds the shaders.

check_box.label: Temporal anti-aliasing (TAA)
check_box.name: fs_fsrendertaa
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Moves the camera by a fraction of a pixel every frame and blends each frame with the ones before it, following the camera's movement and checking depth and the colours around each pixel. Smooths edges, thin geometry, foliage, hair and shimmering highlights far better than FXAA or SMAA, which it replaces while on. Snapshots keep the anti-aliasing chosen in Graphics. Needs HDR. Objects that move by themselves, such as walking avatars, can leave faint trails. About half a millisecond at 1440p. Switching it rebuilds the shaders.

text.name: shadow_alpha_cascades_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many sun shadow maps, nearest first, draw alpha tested casters (leaves, grass, fences, alpha masked materials). In the far maps their shadows are a few texels, and they are a large share of the shadow pass. 4 draws them in all, as before.

check_box.label: Fewer small shadows while the camera moves fast
check_box.name: shadow_reduce_while_moving
check_box.tool_tip: While the camera turns or travels fast, the sun shadow maps past the nearest leave out small objects, and the far ones leave out leaves, grass and fences. Saves a little GPU time while moving the camera, but shadows of small things disappear and pop back a quarter second after the camera stops.

text.name: impostor_update_budget_label

spinner.name: impostor_update_budget
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many avatar impostors may be redrawn per frame because the avatar moved or animated. A missing impostor or an appearance change is still redrawn at once. 0: no limit, as before.

text.name: impostor_min_interval_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Shortest time between redraws of the same avatar impostor for movement or animation, in seconds. Until then it keeps showing its current impostor.

spinner.name: impostor_min_interval
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Shortest time between redraws of the same avatar impostor for movement or animation, in seconds. Until then it keeps showing its current impostor.

text.name: avatar_shadow_distance_label

spinner.name: avatar_shadow_distance
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars and animesh further than this from the camera, with their attachments, cast no shadow. 0 for no limit. Your own avatar always casts.

text.name: avatar_shadow_cascades_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many sun shadow maps, nearest first, other avatars and animesh (with their rigged attachments) cast into. Every map draws each rigged mesh again, so in a crowd the far maps cost the most for the smallest shadows. Avatars further than these maps reach cast no shadow. Your own avatar always casts. 4: all, as before.

Every map draws each rigged mesh again, so in a crowd the far maps cost the most for the smallest shadows. Avatars further than these maps reach cast no shadow. Your own avatar always casts. 4: all, as before.

text.name: spot_shadow_update_interval_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While a projector light and its settings stay unchanged, re-render its shadow only every this many frames. Things moving in its light update with that delay. 1 renders every frame.

panel.text: Update still projector shadows every N frames

spinner.name: spot_shadow_update_interval
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While a projector light and its settings stay unchanged, re-render its shadow only every this many frames. Things moving in its light update with that delay. 1 renders every frame.

check_box.label: Faster sun shadow filtering away from shadow edges
check_box.name: shadow_fast_filter
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sample sun shadows with 3 lookups instead of 5 where the area is clearly fully lit or fully shadowed, and only do all 5 near shadow edges. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Stabilise sun shadow edges while the camera moves
check_box.name: shadow_texel_snap
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Snap each sun shadow cascade to whole shadow map texels, so shadow edges stay put instead of crawling and shimmering while the camera moves or turns. Costs almost nothing.

check_box.label: Order-independent transparency for blended alpha (WBOIT)
check_box.name: alpha_wboit
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Blend transparent surfaces with weighted blended order-independent transparency instead of sorting them. Removes sorting errors between overlapping glass, particles and alpha planes; stacked, nearly opaque layers such as hair can look softer than with sorting.

check_box.label: Soft sun shadows (PCSS)
check_box.name: ShadowPCSS
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Soft sun, moon and projector shadows (percentage-closer soft shadows): shadow edges are sharp where an object touches the ground and soften with the distance to the object casting them. Uses a wider, rotated filter that the shadow blur smooths out. Needs shadows on (Sun/Moon or Sun/Moon + Projectors). Costs GPU time. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: shadow_pcss_light_size_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Size of the light for soft shadows, as a multiple of the sun's real size (scaled by the sky's sun scale; the moon uses the same size). Larger values give wider, softer shadow edges away from the casting object. 1 is the real sun.

spinner.name: shadow_pcss_light_size
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Size of the light for soft shadows, as a multiple of the sun's real size (scaled by the sky's sun scale; the moon uses the same size). Larger values give wider, softer shadow edges away from the casting object. 1 is the real sun.

check_box.label: Blur soft shadow edges on screen
check_box.name: shadow_screen_filter
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With soft sun shadows on: look the shadow up with a narrow, cheap filter and blur it on the screen as wide as its soft edge, without blurring across the edges of objects. Smoother wide shadow edges for fewer shadow map lookups. Needs the shadow blur (Shadow blur size above 0). Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Smooth them over several frames
check_box.name: shadow_screen_filter_temporal
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Blend the blurred sun shadow with the last frames, following the camera, to remove the remaining grain of soft shadow edges. Dropped where another surface was seen before, and held close to the current shadow so moving shadows don't leave trails. Uses two more screen sized buffers.

check_box.label: Sun shadow bias from the surface's slope
check_box.name: shadow_slope_bias
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Measure how steep each surface is from the depth of the pixels around it, instead of from its normal map, when keeping sun shadows from shadowing their own surface. Removes shadow acne and leaks on bumpy, normal mapped walls and floors, and lets the fixed bias below be smaller so shadows sit closer to the objects casting them. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: shadow_slope_bias_constant_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Share of the fixed sun shadow bias and offset kept while the bias follows the surface's slope. Lower values put shadows closer to their casters; raise it if flat surfaces facing the sun show speckles. Default 0.5.

spinner.name: shadow_slope_bias_constant
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Share of the fixed sun shadow bias and offset kept while the bias follows the surface's slope. Lower values put shadows closer to their casters; raise it if flat surfaces facing the sun show speckles. Default 0.5.

check_box.label: Sun shadow bias in metres in every cascade
check_box.name: fs_fsrendershadowbiasmetric
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Keep sun shadows from shadowing their own surface with a fixed distance in metres in every shadow cascade, instead of a fixed share of each cascade's depth, which is a few centimetres close by but a metre or more for distant shadows: their shadows sit away from distant posts, trunks and walls. With this on they stay attached.

text.name: fs_fsrendershadowbiasmetres_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The distance, in metres, a sun shadow is kept off the surface it falls on. Raise it if surfaces in the sun show speckles or stripes; lower it if small objects' shadows start a little away from them. Default 0.05.

spinner.name: fs_fsrendershadowbiasmetres
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The distance, in metres, a sun shadow is kept off the surface it falls on. Raise it if surfaces in the sun show speckles or stripes; lower it if small objects' shadows start a little away from them. Default 0.05.

text.name: fs_fsrendershadowbiastexels_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Distant shadow cascades have coarser texels; this many texels of a cascade are used instead when that is more than the distance above. Raise it if only distant surfaces show speckles. Default 1.

spinner.name: fs_fsrendershadowbiastexels
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Distant shadow cascades have coarser texels; this many texels of a cascade are used instead when that is more than the distance above. Raise it if only distant surfaces show speckles. Default 1.

button.name: reset_fs_heading_shadows
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Shadows" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Merge shadow draw calls
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowmergedbatches
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends the opaque shadow casters of each shadow pass as fewer, larger draw calls. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in scenes with many objects.

check_box.label: Cache static far shadows
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Keeps the shadows of buildings and terrain in the two far sun shadow maps between frames and only redraws moving things into them. Needs 'Snap sun shadows to texels' (FSRenderShadowTexelSnap). Uses one extra depth buffer per far shadow map.

text.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachesunangle_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the static far shadow cache, the far shadows follow the sun in steps of this many degrees, 0 to 2. Larger steps redraw the cache less often under a moving sun.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachesunangle
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the static far shadow cache, the far shadows follow the sun in steps of this many degrees, 0 to 2. Larger steps redraw the cache less often under a moving sun.

check_box.label: Keep far shadow maps still in a busy view
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachestable
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs Cache static far shadows. Lets the far shadow cache be reused while avatars move in view: a far shadow map stays where it is while its part of the view still fits inside it, and objects that only change colour or texture no longer make the cache redraw. Shadows look the same. 'Log shadow batch statistics' shows how often the cache is reused, and why it is redrawn.

check_box.label: Ignore changes that can't show in the far shadows
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachefilter
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs Cache static far shadows. The far shadow cache is no longer redrawn when a moving object only passes through a part of the scene, or when an object too small to cast into the far shadow maps changes. Shadows look the same.

check_box.label: Keep objects that keep changing out of the far shadow cache
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowstaticcachedemote
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs Cache static far shadows. An object that makes the far shadow cache redraw again and again (3 times in 10 seconds while the camera is still), or that spins or is flexible, is drawn with the moving objects instead, as the viewer does for objects that move. After it has been still for a minute (longer each time it starts again) it goes back into the cache. Shadows look the same.

check_box.label: Draw sun shadow cascades in one pass
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowsinglepass
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends buildings, objects, rigged mesh and alpha masked surfaces to the sun shadow maps once instead of once per shadow cascade; the graphics card copies each to every cascade it reaches. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs a graphics card and driver that can pick the viewport in the vertex shader (most NVIDIA and AMD cards with current drivers); otherwise nothing changes. Uses one extra depth buffer the size of the four sun shadow maps.

check_box.label: Keep still projector shadows
check_box.name: fs_fsperfspotshadowcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A projector's shadow is only redrawn when something it shows can have changed: the light moved or changed, objects in its cone were added, removed or changed detail, or an avatar or moving object is inside its cone. Otherwise the last shadow is kept, and it is redrawn at least once a second anyway. Saves the culling and drawing of every shadowed projector that only lights static scenery.

check_box.label: Keep projector shadows of static objects
check_box.name: fs_fsperfspotshadowsplit
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs Keep still projector shadows. A projector with avatars or moving objects in its cone keeps the shadow of its static objects and terrain, and each frame only culls and draws the avatars, attachments, animesh, moving objects, trees and grass over it. Saves most of the main thread time of projectors lighting people. Uses one extra depth buffer per shadowed projector. Translucent parts of avatars stay grey in coloured projector shadows.

check_box.name: fs_fsrendercloudshadows

check_box.label: Smooth shadow fade
check_box.name: fs_fsrendershadowsmoothfade
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sun shadows fade out smoothly towards the shadow distance, and the change between shadow cascades is dithered so there is no visible line where shadow quality changes.

text.name: fs_fsrendershadowfadelength_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Part of the shadow distance over which shadows fade out at its far end.

spinner.name: fs_fsrendershadowfadelength
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Part of the shadow distance over which shadows fade out at its far end.

text.name: fs_fsrendershadowcascadeband_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Where two sun shadow cascades meet, both are blended (or dithered with smooth shadow fade) over this fraction of the distance either side of the change. 0.25 is the standard width; 0.1 leaves a much narrower band of dither or double lookups and gives each cascade a little more detail. Wider hides the change in shadow sharpness better.

spinner.name: fs_fsrendershadowcascadeband
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Where two sun shadow cascades meet, both are blended (or dithered with smooth shadow fade) over this fraction of the distance either side of the change. 0.25 is the standard width; 0.1 leaves a much narrower band of dither or double lookups and gives each cascade a little more detail. Wider hides the change in shadow sharpness better.

button.name: reset_fs_heading_coloured_shadows
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Coloured shadows" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Coloured shadows through transparent surfaces
check_box.name: fs_fsrendercoloredshadows
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sunlight passing through stained glass, tinted windows and other alpha-blended surfaces takes on their colour, in proportion to their opacity. Works up to the second sun shadow split (the nearest few tens of metres). Uses two extra textures the size of the shadow maps (about 8 MB each at 1920x1080 with shadow resolution 1) and redraws transparent objects into the two nearest shadow maps. Needs sun shadows.

text.name: fs_fsrendercoloredshadowabsorption_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much light an opaque-looking transparent surface also blocks. 0 only tints the light; 1 lets a fully opaque surface block it completely. Clear glass is unaffected either way.

spinner.name: fs_fsrendercoloredshadowabsorption
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How much light an opaque-looking transparent surface also blocks. 0 only tints the light; 1 lets a fully opaque surface block it completely. Clear glass is unaffected either way.

check_box.label: Also for projector lights
check_box.name: fs_fsrendercoloredshadowsprojectors
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Light from shadowed projectors passing through stained glass, tinted windows and other alpha-blended surfaces takes on their colour too. Uses one extra texture per shadowed projector, the size of its shadow map (up to 16 MB each), and redraws transparent objects into each projector shadow map. Needs coloured shadows and projector shadows (Sun/Moon + Projectors).

button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Projector shadows" back to its default value.

text.name: fs_fsrenderspotshadowcount_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many projectors cast shadows at once (2 is the standard viewer, up to 6). Each one past two renders another shadow map every update (see the projector shadow update interval) and uses about 16 MB of video memory at 2048 pixels. Needs projector shadows on.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderspotshadowcount
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many projectors cast shadows at once (2 is the standard viewer, up to 6). Each one past two renders another shadow map every update (see the projector shadow update interval) and uses about 16 MB of video memory at 2048 pixels. Needs projector shadows on.

text.name: fs_renderspotshadowmaxresolution_label
text.tool_tip: Largest width and height, in pixels, of the projector shadow maps, which otherwise follow the screen width. Default 2048. 0: no limit, as standard.

spinner.name: fs_renderspotshadowmaxresolution
spinner.tool_tip: Largest width and height, in pixels, of the projector shadow maps, which otherwise follow the screen width. Default 2048. 0: no limit, as standard.

check_box.label: Photo shadows (blend shadows while the camera is still)
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderphotoshadows
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While the camera is still, and in snapshots, the sun shadows near the camera are drawn every frame with the light from another point of the sun's disc and blended over the frames. In a second or two they settle into the sun's real soft shadow: sharp where things touch, softer the further they fall, with no stair steps. Starts over when the camera moves. Costs nothing while moving; snapshots take longer (see below).

text.name: fs_fsrenderphotoshadowsframes_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many frames photo shadows blend at most while the camera is still. More is smoother; fewer follows the sun and moving shadows sooner.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderphotoshadowsframes
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How many frames photo shadows blend at most while the camera is still. More is smoother; fewer follows the sun and moving shadows sooner.

text.name: fs_fsrenderphotoshadowssnapshotframes_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Frames a snapshot draws before each part it reads, for photo shadows. Each one costs a frame of rendering at the snapshot's size, the snapshot preview included. 0 keeps the normal shadows in snapshots.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderphotoshadowssnapshotframes
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Frames a snapshot draws before each part it reads, for photo shadows. Each one costs a frame of rendering at the snapshot's size, the snapshot preview included. 0 keeps the normal shadows in snapshots.

text.name: fs_fsrenderphotoshadowssoftness_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Size of the sun's disc for photo shadows, times the size the sky draws it with. 1 is the real sun; larger gives softer shadows.

spinner.name: fs_fsrenderphotoshadowssoftness
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Size of the sun's disc for photo shadows, times the size the sky draws it with. 1 is the real sun; larger gives softer shadows.

panel.name: experimental_textures_settings

check_box.label: Keep decoded textures on disk (faster loading on return visits)
check_box.name: decoded_texture_cache
check_box.tool_tip: Stores the pixels of decoded textures so places you return to load them without JPEG2000 decoding. Uses several times more disk space than the regular texture cache. Cleared together with the texture cache.

combo_box.name: decoded_texture_cache_mode
combo_box.tool_tip: A region can take several GB of decoded textures. Listed regions only keeps just the regions named below. Current region only keeps what you see where you are, so relogging or moving around the same region reuses it, and drops it once you are somewhere else. Places visited before only keeps textures that were already in the texture cache, so a first visit writes nothing.

line_editor.name: decoded_texture_cache_regions
line_editor.tool_tip: Region names, separated by commas. Their decoded textures are kept on any visit, not dropped when you leave, and removed last when the cache is full.

text.name: decoded_texture_cache_min_size_label
text.tool_tip: Textures smaller than this (larger side, in pixels) decode quickly enough and are not kept.

check_box.label: Store uncompressed (faster loading, about 1.5x the disk space)
check_box.name: decoded_texture_cache_uncompressed
check_box.tool_tip: Decompressing is most of the cost of loading from the decoded cache, and texture pixels only compress to about 65%. Applies to newly stored textures.

check_box.label: Decode the most important textures first
check_box.name: prioritize_texture_decodes
check_box.tool_tip: Decodes textures in order of importance instead of request order, so what is in front of you sharpens first after a teleport or while moving. Decodes for textures nothing waits for anymore are skipped.

check_box.label: Run texture decode and cache threads at low priority
check_box.name: low_priority_texture_threads
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Texture decoding and caching only use CPU time the main and render threads leave free. Smoother frames while a scene loads, but loading can take longer on CPUs with few cores.

check_box.label: Use the video memory the driver reports for the texture budget
check_box.name: use_live_vram
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. On NVIDIA and AMD, textures are reduced when the GPU itself is running out of video memory, counting everything else using it, instead of using a fixed share of it. Has no effect when the texture memory limit is set manually.

text.name: texture_bias_soft_zone_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How far below the texture memory target textures start being reduced, a little at a time, so memory levels off before it runs out instead of dropping detail all at once. 0.1 starts at 90% of the target. 0 waits until the target is reached.

panel.text: Start reducing textures before memory is full

spinner.name: texture_bias_soft_zone
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How far below the texture memory target textures start being reduced, a little at a time, so memory levels off before it runs out instead of dropping detail all at once. 0.1 starts at 90% of the target. 0 waits until the target is reached.

text.name: texture_vram_target_fraction_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the video memory the driver reports, textures and geometry use at most this share of the card. Higher keeps more textures sharp; too high and the card runs out of memory and pages right after login or a teleport, which stutters and blurs everything. 0.7 is about 11 GB on a 16 GB card. 0 removes this cap.

panel.text: Share of video memory textures may use

spinner.name: texture_vram_target_fraction
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the video memory the driver reports, textures and geometry use at most this share of the card. Higher keeps more textures sharp; too high and the card runs out of memory and pages right after login or a teleport, which stutters and blurs everything. 0.7 is about 11 GB on a 16 GB card. 0 removes this cap.

check_box.label: Streamed texture uploads (PBO)
check_box.name: fs_fsperftextureuploadpbo
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Copies newly loaded textures to the graphics card asynchronously, which can reduce stutter when many textures arrive at once. Only has an effect when textures are not already created on a background thread (usually AMD and Intel graphics). Needs OpenGL 4.4.

text.name: fs_fsperftextureuploadbudgetmb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Spreads bursts of newly loaded textures over several frames so they don't all land in one frame, uploading the most important ones first. Lower is smoother but textures appear more slowly. 0 = no limit. 16 is a good start.

spinner.name: fs_fsperftextureuploadbudgetmb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Spreads bursts of newly loaded textures over several frames so they don't all land in one frame, uploading the most important ones first. Lower is smoother but textures appear more slowly. 0 = no limit. 16 is a good start.

button.name: reset_texture_memory_heading
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Texture memory" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Log texture fetch pipeline diagnostics
check_box.name: texture_fetch_pipeline_diagnostics
check_box.tool_tip: Periodically log a texture HTTP pipeline snapshot for diagnosing stalled texture fetches

check_box.label: Recover stalled texture downloads automatically
check_box.name: texture_fetch_self_heal
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. If textures sit waiting for a download slot while no texture downloads are actually running, give the slots back so loading continues. Logged under Texture.

check_box.label: Reduce textures hidden behind other objects first
check_box.name: fs_fstexturepriorityhiddenfaces
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Textures seen only on surfaces the occlusion test has found hidden behind other objects for a few seconds are treated like textures off screen: when video memory runs short they are reduced first, and they no longer get the close-up boost. Surfaces that come back into view count as visible again at once. Has an effect only while textures are being reduced to save memory.

text.name: fs_fstexturepriorityhiddengrace_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How long, in seconds, a surface must stay hidden behind other objects before its textures are treated like textures off screen. Longer keeps textures sharp behind things passing in front of them.

spinner.name: fs_fstexturepriorityhiddengrace
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. How long, in seconds, a surface must stay hidden behind other objects before its textures are treated like textures off screen. Longer keeps textures sharp behind things passing in front of them.

check_box.label: Choose PBR texture detail from the material's texture repeats
check_box.name: fs_fstexturepriorityglftscale
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Choose the detail of PBR (GLTF) material textures from the repeats of the material's own texture transform, which is what draws them, instead of the face's legacy texture repeats, which PBR materials don't use. Textures repeated many times load less detail, stretched ones more.

check_box.label: Load the textures of small avatar parts (eyes, lips, nails) early
check_box.name: fs_fstextureavatarsmallparts
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Textures load in order of how much of the screen they cover, so tiny avatar parts like eyes load last and are the first to be dropped when video memory runs short, leaving grey eyes. With this on, the textures of attachments in view count as at least the size below, so they load early and stay loaded. Uses a little more video memory.

text.name: fs_fstextureavatarsmallpartssize_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The smallest texture size, in pixels, the textures of attachments in view are loaded at. 128 keeps eyes sharp at a conversation distance.

panel.text: Smallest size for avatar part textures

spinner.name: fs_fstextureavatarsmallpartssize
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The smallest texture size, in pixels, the textures of attachments in view are loaded at. 128 keeps eyes sharp at a conversation distance.

check_box.label: Load textures seen only behind other objects one size smaller
check_box.name: fs_fstextureoccludeddiscard
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A texture whose every surface in view has been hidden behind other objects for a few seconds (the seconds set above, also without that option) is wanted at half its width and height. As soon as any of its surfaces is visible again it counts in full and sharpens as fast as it loads. Saves video memory in busy scenes; it takes effect once textures are being reduced to save memory.

check_box.label: Reduce textures in view gradually when memory runs short
check_box.name: fs_fstexturebiasramp
check_box.tool_tip: When video memory fills up and textures are being reduced, textures in view are reduced a little at a time as memory gets fuller, far away and off to the side ones first. Off: the whole mid and far scene switches between sharp and quarter resolution each time the reduction crosses a fixed point, so textures go soft and sharp again over and over.

check_box.label: Load far material maps one size below their colour texture
check_box.name: fs_fstexturematerialmapreduce
check_box.tool_tip: Normal, specular and metallic-roughness maps on surfaces further away than the distance below load at half the width and height of their colour texture. Their fine detail is hardly visible that far away, and the video memory saved lets colour textures everywhere stay sharp. Not added on top of the option above for textures behind other objects.

text.name: fs_fstexturematerialmapdistance_label

spinner.name: fs_fstexturematerialmapdistance
spinner.tool_tip: Surfaces further from the camera than this, in metres, load their normal, specular and metallic-roughness maps one size smaller. 16 matches the distance within which textures get the close-up boost.

check_box.label: Release video memory of textures no longer on any surface
check_box.name: fs_fstexturereleasefaceless
check_box.tool_tip: Textures that have been on no surface for the seconds below, such as those of the region you just teleported from, of objects that went out of view, or kept by a cached material, are shrunk to their smallest size a few at a time instead of holding their video memory until they are dropped or memory runs out. That memory goes to what is in view, so it loads sharper. The UI, HUDs, avatars, the sky, terrain, sculpts, projectors, particles, previews and media keep theirs. A texture that comes back into view loads again as usual.

text.name: fs_fstexturereleasefacelessdelay_label

They are never hidden by the occlusion test while in view; out of view your worn objects keep following your body, keep their mesh detail and keep their textures at the size they would have close to the camera instead of being reduced first. check_box.label: Keep avatar ranking steady while object updates arrive
check_box.name: perf_avatarrankhysteresis

check_box.label: Reuse rigged mesh joint matrices until the skeleton moves
check_box.name: perf_riggedpalettecache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Build each rigged mesh's joint matrix palette once per skeleton update and reuse it in every render pass (camera, shadows, probes), instead of rebuilding it for each pass.

check_box.name: perf_attachmentextentscache

check_box.label: Build rigged mesh skinning matrices on the avatar workers
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelskinpalettes
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With 'Update other avatars on worker threads' on, build the skinning matrices of each avatar's rigged attachments on its worker too, right after its pose, instead of on the main thread while drawing. check_box.label: Skin rigged meshes once per frame
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinonce

Meshes that just came into view or changed, and the GPU driven rigged draws, are skinned as before. Needs OpenGL 4.3. Nothing should look different; compare the frame rate in a crowd with it on and off. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: Only Bakes on Mesh is skin
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinbakesonly
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Only rigged mesh faces that show your avatar's bakes (Bakes on Mesh) count as skin. Mesh clothing, hair, jewellery and animesh attachments (ears, tails) are never treated as skin, whatever their colour; the system avatar still is. Applier skins (textures put on the body directly, not Bakes on Mesh) need this off, and are then judged by colour as before.

check_box.label: Detect skin by its material too
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskindetectmaterial
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Judge what is skin by its material as well as its colour: skin is non-metallic with medium roughness, while most cloth is rougher and jewellery metallic or very glossy. Keeps scattering off beige clothing and lets the colour test take in pale, very dark and fantasy skins. The system avatar's bakes have no material, so there colour still decides. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

text.name: fs_fsrenderskintonerange_label

text.name: fs_fsrenderskinhairfilter_label

A Bakes on Mesh hair base, brows and lashes are painted into the head's bake, so they are the same surface as the skin; at 1 they get no skin sheen, highlight, scattering or backlit glow, so a hair base no longer looks glossy. Painted hair is recognised by its strands and by being darker than any skin. 0 treats it as skin, as before.

check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskindualspecular

Skin shines with two highlights in one: a sharp one from its oily surface and a broad, soft one from fine wrinkles and pores, as film and game character shading does. Applies to the sun and local lights, at skin's own reflectance and with the same total brightness as one highlight. Legacy skins without a specular map get a skin highlight too. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.name: fs_fsrenderskinwarmshadows

check_box.label: Soft rim sheen on skin

check_box.name: perf_alpharesortonly
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. When the camera turns, re-order only the transparent faces of each group for correct blending, instead of rebuilding the group's geometry.

check_box.label: Spread geometry rebuilds over frames and defer off-screen ones
check_box.name: perf_rebuildtimebudget
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Limit how long geometry rebuilds may take each frame and rebuild groups and particles that are off screen only once they come into view.

check_box.label: Fit shadow maps using the camera's visible objects
check_box.name: perf_shadowpointcloudfromcull
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Work out the shadow map bounds from the objects the camera already found visible, instead of searching the scene again for every shadow cascade.

check_box.label: Sort sun shadow casters once for all cascades
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowsharedstatesort
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the shared sun shadow cull (RenderShadowCullMode 1), the geometry rebuilds and the collection of each object group's draw calls run once per shadow update instead of once per cascade; each cascade only takes the groups in its own frustum. Shadows look the same; saves main thread time in busy scenes. Does nothing with RenderShadowCullMode 0.

check_box.label: Faster occlusion queries (NVIDIA)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfrepresentativefragmenttest
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Lets NVIDIA Turing and newer graphics cards stop drawing an occlusion test box as soon as one pixel of it is found visible, which makes the hidden-object checks cheaper. Visibility results stay the same. Has no effect on other graphics cards.

check_box.label: Leave transparent faces without glow out of the glow pass
check_box.name: fs_fsperfalphaglowskip
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Transparent faces get drawn a second time for glow whenever any face near them has glow, even when they have none themselves. Skip that second draw for faces without glow; it adds nothing to the picture.

check_box.label: Test for hidden objects after foliage, avatars and animesh are drawn
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderocclusionafteropaque
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The occlusion test that skips hidden groups of objects runs after every opaque surface is drawn, so alpha masked surfaces (foliage, fences), grass, trees, avatars and animesh hide what is behind them too. Draws less in busy scenes. Something revealed by a moving avatar or a swaying plant can show up a frame late.

check_box.label: Light particles cheaply (fog and smoke)
check_box.name: fs_fsrendercheapparticles
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Smoke, fog and other particles take the ambient light of the sky probe instead of searching the nearby reflection probes, one sun shadow sample instead of a filtered set, and the four local lights nearest the camera instead of seven. Thick fog, which stacks many large particles on every pixel, costs much less on the graphics card. Fog can look slightly different near local lights and inside buildings with their own reflection probes.

check_box.label: Light the transparent parts of distant avatars cheaply
check_box.name: fs_fsrendercheapavataralpha
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. The transparent parts of other avatars farther away than the distance below (hair, lace, sheer clothing, PBR blend) are lit like cheap particles: the light of the sky probe instead of the nearby reflection probes, one sun shadow sample instead of a filtered set, and the four local lights nearest the camera instead of seven. Fog stays the same. Your own avatar, nearby avatars and HUDs keep the full lighting. Costs less on the graphics card in crowded places; distant hair can look slightly different near local lights and inside buildings with their own reflection probes.

text.name: fs_fsrendercheapavataralphadistance_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars farther from the camera than this many metres have their transparent parts lit cheaply; nearer ones keep the full lighting.

spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars farther from the camera than this many metres have their transparent parts lit cheaply; nearer ones keep the full lighting.

check_box.label: Look for nearby lights 10 times a second
check_box.name: perf_lightrescanthrottle
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Rescan the scene for the nearest local lights 10 times a second, or when the camera moves, instead of every frame.

check_box.label: Skip mirror cube faces that cannot be seen
check_box.name: perf_heroprobeskiphiddenfaces
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Do not render the sides of a mirror's reflection cube that face away from the mirror surface or, for a flat mirror, that no reflection off it can reach (usually 3 or 4 of the 6). When the sides left fit in the faces per frame the mirror update rate allows, they are all rendered every frame, so the reflection doesn't lag or show seams.

check_box.label: Render flat mirrors as one sharp planar view
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermirrorplanar
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A flat mirror is rendered once per frame as a single view fitted to the part of it you can see, at a resolution that follows its size on screen, instead of the six sides of a reflection cube a few at a time. The reflection is much sharper, lines up exactly, does not lag behind when you move and costs far less. Curved or thick mirrors keep the cube. Rebuilds the shaders.

text.name: fs_fsrendermirrorplanarscale_label

check_box.label: Update small planar mirrors less often
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermirrorplanaradaptiverate

check_box.label: Show avatars in every mirror
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermirroravatars
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars (your own included), animesh and particles show in every mirror, not only in mirrors whose creator ticked Dynamic. Costs more where a mirror sees many avatars.

check_box.name: perf_probeuniformcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Do not update the mirror (hero) probe data a second time in each render pass; the reflection probe update already includes it.

check_box.label: Batch local light drawing
check_box.name: fs_fsperfbatchedlocallights
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws point lights in a few instanced calls instead of one call per light, cutting CPU time where hundreds of lights are visible (clubs, cities). Lighting should look the same. Spotlights and projectors are unchanged. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Batch projector drawing
check_box.name: fs_fsperfbatchedspotlights
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws projectors (spotlights) that are not casting shadows in a few instanced calls per projector texture instead of one call per light, and draws the ones the camera is inside of over their light volume instead of the whole screen. Cuts CPU and GPU time in crowds full of projector facelights. Lighting should look the same; shadowed projectors are unchanged. Rebuilds shaders when changed.

check_box.label: Cull sun shadow maps on worker threads (casters found per map only)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelshadowcull
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Works out which objects fall into each sun shadow map on several CPU cores at once instead of one map after another on the main thread. Shadows look the same; saves main thread time in busy scenes. Only works with Shadows > Find sun shadow casters set to Separately per map: with Once for all maps there is a single search already, and this does nothing.

check_box.label: Build object geometry on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelgeometry
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Fills the vertex data of rezzing and changing objects on several CPU cores instead of only the main thread. Reduces hitches on region arrival, teleports and heavy rezzing. Looks exactly the same as when off.

check_box.label: Verify threaded geometry (slow, debug)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelgeometryverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug aid: builds the geometry a second time on the main thread and logs any difference to the threaded result. Costs more than it saves; for testing only.

text.name: fs_fsperfparallelgeometryminverts_label

spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A geometry rebuild uses the worker threads only when it has at least this many vertices; smaller ones are built on the main thread, where waking the workers would cost more than it saves.

check_box.label: Animate avatars on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelavatarupdate
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Evaluates the animations of all visible avatars of a frame in parallel on worker threads instead of one after another on the main thread. Helps most in crowded places. Your own avatar stays on the main thread.

check_box.label: Verify parallel avatar animation
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelavatarupdateverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug check: recomputes the avatar joints serially after the worker threads and logs any difference. Costs extra CPU time, only for testing.

check_box.label: Cull the main view and reflection probes on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelmaincull
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Works out which objects are in view (main camera and reflection probe updates) on several CPU cores at once instead of only on the main thread. The scene looks the same; saves main thread time in busy scenes.

check_box.label: Check worker view culls against the old cull
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelmaincullverify
check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Also runs the old view cull and writes any difference to the log. Slower; only for testing.

check_box.label: Build render lists on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsort
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Collects the draw lists of each camera (main view, shadow cascades, probes) on worker threads in postSort. Same result as before, less main thread time in busy places.

check_box.label: Verify parallel render lists
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsortverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug: also builds the render lists serially and logs any difference. Slower; for testing only.

text.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsortmingroups_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Views with fewer visible groups than this build their render lists on the main thread, where the worker hand-off would cost more than it saves.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfparallelpostsortmingroups
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Views with fewer visible groups than this build their render lists on the main thread, where the worker hand-off would cost more than it saves.

check_box.label: Texture priorities on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparalleltexturepriority
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Computes how sharp each texture needs to be (face screen areas and texture virtual sizes) on worker threads instead of the main thread. Helps in busy places with many textures loaded.

check_box.label: Verify parallel texture priorities
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparalleltexturepriorityverify
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Debug: also computes texture priorities the old way and logs any difference. Costs more than either alone.

check_box.label: Disk cache lookups on a separate thread
check_box.name: fs_fsperfdiskthread
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Looks assets up in the disk cache on a separate low priority thread instead of the main thread, and reads them once there so the main thread's later read comes from memory. Cached animations go through the same lookup. Helps against hitches when content arrives in bursts and the cache is on a slow disk or scanned by antivirus software. A cached asset becomes ready about a frame later.

check_box.label: Free object geometry on a worker thread
check_box.name: fs_fsperfbackgroundvolumefree
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Frees the geometry of objects that go away (a region leaving view, objects changing detail level) on a worker thread instead of the main thread. A region going out of range frees thousands of shapes at once, which took a few hundred milliseconds of the frame.

check_box.label: Run audio (OpenAL) on its own thread
check_box.name: fs_fsperfaudiothread
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Make every OpenAL call on an audio thread of its own instead of the main thread. A call that waits inside OpenAL (its locks, the mixer, an output device being reopened) then can't hold up a frame. Sounds start up to a few milliseconds later. Takes effect after a restart.

How much of the decoder's large working buffers each texture decode thread keeps for its next decode, in MB, instead of handing them back to Windows and getting them back fresh every time. Saves the bursts of page faults that make the whole computer sluggish while many textures decode at once (logging in, arriving somewhere). 0 turns it off. Takes effect after a restart.

button.label: Reset to default

check_box.label: Draw shadow casters with multi-draw indirect
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivendraws
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends the opaque buildings and objects of each shadow map to the graphics card as one multi-draw call instead of one call per object batch, from a copy of their positions kept in video memory. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Works together with 'Draw sun shadow cascades in one pass'. Needs OpenGL 4.3 (most NVIDIA, AMD and Intel cards with current drivers; not macOS); otherwise nothing changes.

check_box.label: Verify multi-draw shadows (slow)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivendrawsverify
check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Draws the shadow casters a second time the old way and logs any place where the result would differ, plus draw statistics every 10 seconds. Slows rendering down; for testing only.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivendrawsarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: Most video memory the copy of the shadow casters' positions may use. Casters that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivendrawsarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: Most video memory the copy of the shadow casters' positions may use. Casters that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: GPU-driven PBR surfaces
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbr
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws static opaque PBR (GLTF material) surfaces with a few large multi-draw calls out of a shared vertex arena instead of one draw call each. Looks the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs OpenGL 4.3. Uses up to the arena size below of video memory. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: Bindless PBR textures
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrbindless
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With GPU-driven PBR surfaces: uses bindless textures (GL_ARB_bindless_texture) so surfaces with different materials share one draw call. Looks the same; saves more CPU time. Not used where the driver doesn't support it properly. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven PBR surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven PBR surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: GPU-driven legacy surfaces
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenlegacy
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws static opaque non-PBR surfaces (simple, alpha masked and fullbright) with a few large multi-draw calls out of a shared vertex arena, with bindless textures, instead of one draw call and several texture binds each. Looks the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs OpenGL 4.3 and bindless textures (NVIDIA GPUs only). Uses up to the arena size below of video memory. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenlegacyarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenlegacyarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: Group PBR and legacy material draws
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrgroupruns
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to GPU-driven PBR surfaces and GPU-driven legacy material surfaces: draws them grouped instead of in the stock order. PBR: every surface with bindless textures in one multi-draw, the others one run per material. Legacy materials: every GPU-driven surface in one multi-draw. The surfaces drawn the old way follow. Far fewer draw calls and texture binds in busy scenes. Only where two surfaces lie at exactly the same depth can the other one show.

check_box.label: GPU-driven legacy material surfaces
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterials
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws static opaque surfaces with legacy normal or specular maps (or shine on a material) with a few large multi-draw calls out of a shared vertex arena, with bindless textures, instead of one draw call, several texture binds and material settings each. Looks the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Needs OpenGL 4.3 and bindless textures (NVIDIA GPUs only). Uses up to the arena size below of video memory. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterialsarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy material surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterialsarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the GPU-driven legacy material surfaces may use for their copy of the vertex data, 16 to 2048 MB. Surfaces that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: Draw alpha tested shadow casters with multi-draw indirect
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenshadowalpha
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Sends the alpha tested shadow casters (leaves, fences, grass, cut-out textures, alpha masked PBR materials) of each shadow map to the graphics card as one multi-draw call with bindless textures, instead of one call and several texture binds per object batch. Shadows look the same; saves CPU time in busy scenes. Works together with 'Draw sun shadow cascades in one pass'; checked by 'Verify multi-draw shadows'. Needs OpenGL 4.3 and bindless textures (NVIDIA GPUs only); otherwise nothing changes. Rebuilds shaders.

text.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenshadowalphaarenamb_label
text.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the copy of the alpha tested shadow casters' vertex data may use, 16 to 2048 MB. Casters that don't fit are drawn the old way.

spinner.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenshadowalphaarenamb
spinner.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Most video memory the copy of the alpha tested shadow casters' vertex data may use, 16 to 2048 MB. Casters that don't fit are drawn the old way.

check_box.label: Rigged mesh joint matrices in one buffer per frame
check_box.name: fs_fsperfriggedpalettebuffer
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Write each rigged mesh's joint matrices once a frame into one buffer that every program, pass and shadow cascade reads, instead of uploading them to each program that draws the mesh. Saves main and render thread time with many avatars around; nothing looks different. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: GPU driven draws for rigged meshes
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenrigged
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draw the opaque rigged meshes of the G-buffer pass (bodies, clothes, attachments) as a few multi-draw calls, like the GPU driven paths above do for static objects, instead of one draw call each with its own state changes. Needs the joint matrix buffer. Saves main and render thread time with many avatars around; nothing looks different. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: GPU driven draws for alpha blended objects
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenalpha
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. NVIDIA only. In the alpha pass, draw runs of consecutive plain alpha, fullbright alpha and legacy material alpha draws that share their shader and blend mode as one multi-draw call each, in the same order, so blending stays exactly as before. Rigged ones too with the joint matrix buffer and GPU driven rigged draws on. Saves main and render thread time with many avatars around; nothing looks different. Rebuilds shaders.

check_box.label: GPU-driven draws: upload ring
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenuploadring
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to every GPU-driven option above. Their per draw data goes into a few large buffers that take turns over three frames, instead of each pass asking the driver for 4 to 5 new buffers every time it draws. With the render thread off and OpenGL 4.4 the buffers are written directly. Less driver work; nothing looks different. The FSGPUDrivenUpload log line shows what it does.

check_box.label: GPU-driven draws: one matrix table per view and frame
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivensharedmatrices
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to every GPU-driven option above. The passes of a frame that draw with the same camera (opaque, rigged and alpha; the passes of one shadow map) share their table of object matrices, so each object's matrices are worked out and sent to the graphics card once instead of once per pass. Saves main thread time in busy scenes; the same math, so nothing looks different. The FSGPUDrivenUpload log line shows what it does.

check_box.label: GPU-driven draws: keep built passes while the scene holds still
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenbuildcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Applies to the GPU-driven shadow caster, legacy and legacy material draws (not rigged). A pass that is given the same objects as in the last frame draws the commands it built then again instead of building them anew; only its texture handles and copies are checked and its matrices looked up again. Saves main thread time while you and the scene hold still, most of all in busy scenes; a pass whose objects changed is built as before, so nothing looks different. The FSGPUDrivenBuild log line (with the GPU-driven statistics on) shows how often it helps.

check_box.label: GPU occlusion culling for GPU-driven objects
check_box.name: fs_fsrendergpuocclusionculling
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs GPU driven draws for PBR objects; also culls what the GPU-driven legacy and material passes draw. In the main view, the graphics card leaves out static objects that are hidden behind what is already drawn: it first draws what was visible last frame, then tests every other object's box against that depth and draws the ones that turned out visible, so nothing pops in late. Saves graphics card time in dense scenes with walls and buildings in front of other objects; little in open views. Rigged meshes are tested with their avatar's bounds, generously padded (never your own avatar's). Alpha, shadows, reflection probes and mirrors are drawn as before. Turning it on rebuilds the scene's geometry once. The FSGPUOcclusion log line shows how much it culls.

check_box.label: Merge post-processing passes
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermergepostpasses
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws post-processing passes that can be one as one full screen pass, with the same math: the sun rays (or underwater rays) together with the volumetric projector light when both are on, and the vignette inside the lens effects pass when both are on. Saves a full screen pass for each pair, about 0.05 to 0.2 ms of graphics card time at 1440p. The picture stays the same apart from the last bit of rounding.

check_box.label: Run OpenGL on a separate render thread (restart required)
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderthread
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Windows only, takes effect after a restart. The main thread hands its OpenGL work to a render thread, which talks to the graphics driver while the main thread already prepares the next frame. Can raise the frame rate when the main thread is the bottleneck. The picture is the same; if something renders wrongly or the viewer stalls, turn it off.

check_box.label: Compile shaders in parallel

check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Shorter pauses when graphics settings change and shaders are rebuilt, because the graphics driver compiles them on several threads at once. Needs a driver that supports parallel shader compile (current NVIDIA and AMD drivers, Mesa). Without that support nothing changes. Applies from the next shader rebuild.

check_box.label: Compress uploaded textures on several cores
check_box.name: fs_fsperfparalleltextureencode
check_box.tool_tip: The viewer freezes while it compresses a texture for upload, about a second per large texture, and a material upload compresses up to four. With this on, each texture is compressed on several cores and the maps of a material at the same time, so the freeze is several times shorter. Applies to textures, materials, snapshots and mesh textures.

check_box.label: Sort only open inventory folders right away
check_box.name: fs_fsperfinventorylazysort
check_box.tool_tip: Opening the inventory, switching its tabs or changing the sort order sorted every folder at once, a freeze of a few hundred milliseconds with large inventories. With this on, open folders are sorted right away and each closed folder when you open it. With folders sorted by date everything is still sorted at once, since that order depends on what is inside them.

check_box.label: Check sound mute and parcel rules 4 times a second
check_box.name: perf_audiothrottlechecks
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Re-check whether each sound source is muted or allowed by parcel rules 4 times a second, or right away when the mute list, parcel or your position changes, instead of every frame.

check_box.label: Update hidden inventory panels less often
check_box.name: perf_inventoryidlethrottle
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Inventory panels that are not on screen update their folder views twice a second instead of every frame.

check_box.label: Reuse the hover pick while still
check_box.name: fs_fsperfhoverpickthrottle
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While the mouse, its buttons and the camera stay still, the viewer reuses what it found under the mouse for up to a tenth of a second instead of casting a ray through the scene every frame. Something moving under a still mouse is noticed within that time.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_fs_heading_scene_updates
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Scene updates" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Vertex array objects
check_box.name: fs_fsperfvertexarrayobjects
check_box.tool_tip: Vertex buffers drawn more than once keep a vertex array object per shader layout, so a draw binds one object instead of setting up its buffers and attributes again. Off: the standard path.

check_box.label: Bind textures straight to their unit (OpenGL 4.5)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfdsatexturebinds
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Draws bind their textures with one call that names the texture unit, instead of switching the active unit first: about one OpenGL call fewer per texture bound. Only on OpenGL 4.5 (not macOS). Off: the standard path.

check_box.label: Rebuild nearest objects first
check_box.name: fs_fsperfrebuildnearestfirst
check_box.tool_tip: When geometry updates (level of detail changes, new objects) can't all be done in one frame, do the ones in view and nearest the camera first, so the objects around you sharpen before distant ones. Off: the standard order.

check_box.label: Share sun shadows between probe faces
check_box.name: fs_renderreflectionprobesharedshadows
check_box.tool_tip: Render the sun shadows once per reflection probe update and share them between its 12 face renders, instead of rendering them for every face. Off: the standard path.

text.name: fs_renderreflectionproberefreshframeinterval_label
text.tool_tip: While refreshing a reflection probe that is already complete, render one cube face every this many frames. New probes, the sky probe and moving probes still update every frame. 1 is standard.

spinner.tool_tip: While refreshing a reflection probe that is already complete, render one cube face every this many frames. New probes, the sky probe and moving probes still update every frame. 1 is standard.

text.name: fs_renderreflectionprobeminrefresh_label
text.tool_tip: A complete reflection probe that doesn't move is not re-rendered until this many seconds after its last refresh. Sky changes still refresh it. 0 is standard.

spinner.name: fs_renderreflectionprobeminrefresh
spinner.tool_tip: A complete reflection probe that doesn't move is not re-rendered until this many seconds after its last refresh. Sky changes still refresh it. 0 is standard.

text.name: fs_renderhiddenavatarupdateperiod_label
text.tool_tip: Avatars outside the camera view are fully updated every this many frames (at most 2 with sun shadows on). 1 is standard, every frame.

spinner.name: fs_renderhiddenavatarupdateperiod
spinner.tool_tip: Avatars outside the camera view are fully updated every this many frames (at most 2 with sun shadows on). 1 is standard, every frame.

check_box.label: Decode cached objects on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfthreadedobjectupdates
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While objects around you are created from the object cache (arriving somewhere, logging in, turning around), the ones coming up next are decoded on worker threads: their shape parameters and their texture faces. The main thread then only applies them, at the same moment and in the same order as before, and decodes anything the workers haven't reached yet itself. Updates sent straight from the region (movement, changes, removals) are handled as before. The result is identical; the gain is small.

check_box.label: Build prim shapes for a new level of detail on worker threads
check_box.name: fs_fsperfthreadedgeometry
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. When a prim switches to a level of detail whose shape hasn't been built yet (arriving somewhere, moving the camera through a build), the shape is built on a worker thread instead of the main thread, and the prim keeps its current detail for one more frame meanwhile. Sculpts, meshes, flexible prims, HUDs and what you are editing are handled as before. Off: the standard path.

check_box.label: Re-check settled textures less often while the camera is still
check_box.name: fs_fsperftextureupdateslice
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While the camera stands still, a texture that is already loaded at the sharpness it needs and isn't on anything moving has its priority worked out on one pass of the texture sweep out of every few instead of on every pass. Textures still loading, sharpening or shrinking, avatar, UI and sculpt textures, projector textures and textures on moving objects keep the normal rate, and so does everything while the camera moves or turns, during a teleport and after the texture memory limit tightens. Saves main thread time in a still scene with many textures.

text.name: fs_fsperftextureupdateslicepasses_label
text.tool_tip: A settled texture is looked at on one pass of the texture sweep out of this many (a pass takes 10 to 20 frames). 1 is the normal rate; higher saves more, but with the camera still a moving object coming closer sharpens a little later.

panel.text: Texture sweeps per settled texture check

spinner.name: fs_fsperftextureupdateslicepasses
spinner.tool_tip: A settled texture is looked at on one pass of the texture sweep out of this many (a pass takes 10 to 20 frames). 1 is the normal rate; higher saves more, but with the camera still a moving object coming closer sharpens a little later.

check_box.label: Size internal memory to the graphics card and the scene
check_box.name: fs_fsautosizeresources
check_box.tool_tip: Sizes that used to be fixed follow the graphics card and what the scene actually uses. The GPU-driven draw arenas start at about what they held at most in your last session, make room by dropping copies not drawn for a couple of seconds before they grow, grow in smaller steps once they are large, and give back memory they no longer use after it has been steady for a few minutes while video memory is short. The GPU-driven upload ring is sized for the most a frame needed in the last minute. With live video memory on, the memory kept free for the system (when left at 0) is 12% of the card, between 1.5 and 3 GB. Nothing here changes what is drawn. Off: the fixed sizes as before.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_perf_heading_while_moving
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "While moving" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Lighter frames while walking, running or turning the camera
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderlighterwhilemoving
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Walking and running never counted as moving for the motion throttles, which only reacted to turning faster than 35 degrees a second or travelling faster than 20 m/s, so every step changed object detail, re-rendered the far sun shadows and filled texture memory. This adds a walking tier (walking, running, gentle turns) that the options below use; each must be on as well. Off: everything as before.

check_box.label: Spread detail rebuilds over frames while moving
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermovingrebuildbudget
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While moving, the group rebuild throttle (debug setting FSPerfGroupRebuildBudgetMs) also works at walking speed, with a budget of what the last frame left of the target frame time (the frame rate limit, or 60), at least 1 ms. Bursts of detail changes are spread over several frames instead of 20-30 ms spikes. What is in view and nearest sharpens first.

check_box.label: Hold level of detail changes while moving
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermovinglodhold
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While moving, objects don't drop to a lower level of detail, and only go up once clearly past the threshold (15%), so objects at the edge don't flip back and forth. Held changes are applied once the camera is still. Objects you walk towards may sharpen a moment later; objects behind you keep their detail until you stop.

check_box.label: Fewer small shadows in the far shadow maps while walking
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermovingshadowreduce
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs 'Fewer small shadows while the camera moves fast' (Shadows tab). While walking, running or turning gently, the far sun shadow maps leave out objects twice as small as they otherwise would. Small distant shadows may pop back in when you stop.

check_box.label: Hold the texture discard bias while moving
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermovingtexturebiashold
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While moving, texture memory nearing its limit doesn't raise the discard bias and loaded textures aren't shrunk (each shrunk texture is a new texture, thousands of them mid-walk). The bias carries on once you stop. Running out of memory still lowers texture resolution at once.

check_box.label: Keep the far shadow maps while the view still fits them
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermovingshadowhold
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs 'Update far sun shadows every N frames' above 1 (Shadows tab). Moving 2% of the shadow range or turning 3 degrees used to render every far shadow map, every frame while walking. Now a far map keeps its interval while what the view needs from it (the visible surfaces in its range, with a few texels to spare, and its depth range) still fits inside it; when it doesn't, all are rendered at once as before. Distant moving objects' shadows follow at the interval, as when still.

check_box.label: Keep the far shadow cache while moving
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermovingshadowcache
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Needs 'Cache static far shadows' (Shadows tab). The cache ignores changes of objects too small to cast into it, lets level of detail changes wait while the camera moves (2 seconds at most, or until it stops), keeps its map from shrinking while moving, and is stored while moving. A distant object's shadow may show its previous level of detail for up to 2 seconds.

check_box.label: Don't refresh reflection probes while moving
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermovingprobehold
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. While moving, reflection probes that already have a picture aren't refreshed; they are once you stop. New probes and probes a sky change needs are still captured. Reflections of things that changed while you walked update when you stop.

check_box.label: Read occlusion results without waiting for the render thread
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderasyncocclusionreadback
check_box.tool_tip: With the render thread on: hidden-object test results are read from what the render thread has already collected, never with a read that makes the main thread wait for it. A test it no longer tracks (after a shader build) isn't waited for: its objects show until a new test answers, which can cost a little more drawing for a frame. Off: as before.

button.label: Reset to default
button.name: reset_perf_heading_hitches
button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Hitches" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Keep render thread state over shader builds
check_box.name: fs_fsperfrenderthreadkeepvaostate
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With the render thread on: after a shader build the main thread forgot what it knew of every mesh's buffers and waited for the render thread once for each on its next draw, thousands of waits in one frame. It now keeps what didn't change. The picture is the same; if something renders wrongly after changing a shader setting, turn it off.

check_box.label: Faster clicks on avatars and worn meshes
check_box.name: fs_fsperffastriggedpick
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. A right click on an avatar or a worn mesh (or the edit tools on one) worked out every vertex of every rigged mesh along the mouse ray, a third of a second over a few detailed avatars. Now only the parts the ray can reach are worked out, parts already worked out for the same pose are reused, and a hovered worn mesh is worked out a few times a second at most. What gets clicked is the same.

check_box.label: Grow GPU-driven memory early, one part at a time
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgddarenasmoothgrowth
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. With "Size internal memory to the graphics card and the scene" on: the memory GPU-driven drawing copies meshes into grows before it is full, at the start of a frame, one part at a time and in video memory only. Growing it all at once in a busy scene stalled the viewer for most of a second.

button.tool_tip: Set every option in "Avatar animation detail" back to its default value.

check_box.label: Animate distant avatars at a lower rate
check_box.name: fs_fsperfanimationlod
check_box.tool_tip: EXPERIMENTAL. Avatars that are small on screen (far away, unless the camera is zoomed onto them) work out their animations only every 2nd, 3rd or 4th frame instead of every frame, spread over the frames. They still move and turn smoothly every frame and their animations keep their timing; only the pose itself steps, and never by more than an eighth of a second. Your own avatar, avatars sitting on the same object as you, the avatar you select or focus the camera on, worn animated objects and avatars that just arrived, sat down or stood up stay at every frame, and everyone does in mouselook and while a snapshot window is open. Saves main thread time in crowds; compare the frame rate with it on and off and watch distant dancers.

text.tool_tip: How big an avatar has to be on screen, as a share of the screen height, to be animated every frame. Below it every 2nd frame, below half of it every 3rd, below a quarter every 4th. Larger values throttle more avatars and save more; smaller ones keep more at every frame.

check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Writes OpenGL calls made from the wrong thread, and calls that make the main thread wait for the render thread, to the log. Only for testing.

check_box.label: Log render thread calls per type and per pass
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderthreadcallstats
check_box.tool_tip: Adds two lines to the render thread statistics in the log (every 60 seconds): the OpenGL calls made most per frame, and the calls per frame of each GPU pass. Costs a little main thread time on every call while on.

check_box.label: Log PBR multi-draw statistics and texture handles
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrstats
check_box.tool_tip: Every 10 seconds, logs (FSGPUDrivenPBR) how many PBR batches went out in how many multi-draw calls, why batches were drawn the old way, the arena sizes and the bindless texture handles (made, resident, dropped). No stalls.

check_box.label: Log legacy multi-draw statistics
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenlegacystats
check_box.tool_tip: Every 10 seconds, logs (FSGPUDrivenLegacy) how many legacy batches went out in how many multi-draw calls, why batches were drawn the old way and the arena sizes. No stalls.

check_box.label: Log material multi-draw statistics
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterialsstats
check_box.tool_tip: Every 10 seconds, logs (FSGPUDrivenMaterials) how many material batches went out in how many multi-draw calls, why batches were drawn the old way and the arena sizes, used and allocated. No stalls.

check_box.label: Log shadow batch statistics
check_box.name: fs_fsperfshadowbatchstats
check_box.tool_tip: Every 10 seconds, logs how many opaque shadow batches were drawn in how many draw calls, and how often the far sun cascade cache was reused or drawn again. Works with the shadow options on or off, to compare.

check_box.label: Log skin-once statistics
check_box.name: fs_fsperfskinoncestats
check_box.tool_tip: Every 10 seconds, logs (FSSkinOnce) what 'Skin rigged meshes once per frame' did per frame: meshes and vertices skinned once, how many draws and vertices reused them (passes per vertex skinned once), how many draws skinned in their shader and why, and the memory used. No stalls.

check_box.label: Verify PBR multi-draws (slow)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenpbrverify
check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Draws the PBR batches a second time the old way and logs any place where the result would differ, plus statistics every 10 seconds. Stalls the GPU; for testing only.

check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Draws the legacy batches a second time the old way and logs any place where the result would differ, plus statistics every 10 seconds. Stalls the GPU; for testing only.

check_box.label: Verify material multi-draws (slow)
check_box.name: fs_fsperfgpudrivenmaterialsverify
check_box.tool_tip: Debug. Draws the material batches a second time the old way and logs any place where the result would differ, plus statistics every 10 seconds. Stalls the GPU; for testing only.

check_box.label: Log repeated meshes, hidden geometry and texture use
check_box.name: fs_fsdiagnosticsgpuwork
check_box.tool_tip: Diagnostics. Every 10 seconds, logs (FSGPUWork) how many objects share one mesh or prim shape and the geometry their copies take, how much of what is in view the occlusion queries hide and how much of what is drawn is behind the finished depth anyway (one box test per object on one frame), and texture memory by whether its faces are visible, hidden or off screen. Each log costs a few milliseconds once.

check_box.label: Log UI frame cap statistics
check_box.name: fs_fsrenderuicapstats
check_box.tool_tip: Every 10 seconds, logs (FSUICap) how often the cached UI was composited and redrawn and why, how many redraws had views change while drawn, how many frames drew the UI directly and why, and how many times its buffer was allocated. A few counters per frame.

check_box.label: Log what the lighter-while-moving options do
check_box.name: fs_fsrendermotionstats
check_box.tool_tip: Every 10 seconds, logs (FSMotion) the time spent still, walking and moving fast, the rebuild budget while moving, level of detail changes held and caught up, texture bias holds, far shadow maps held or rendered and why, static shadow cache filtering, reflection probe refreshes put off, and occlusion results read without and with waiting. A few counters per frame.
